# Problem statement

The `a-r` (audit reject) chord in herdr fails with `bash: -c: unexpected EOF while looking for matching '`'` when the user-entered rejection reason contains an apostrophe. The `substituteIdentifiers` function in `form-dialog.ts` performs raw string replacement, inserting user text into a shell command template where the placeholder sits inside single quotes — an unescaped apostrophe terminates the quote early.

## Headline

Fix `a-r` audit reject shortcut to properly shell-escape user-entered reason text, preventing bash parsing errors when the reason contains apostrophes or other shell metacharacters.

## Users

- **Primary**: Operators who reject audited work items via `a-r` and need to explain why.
- **Secondary**: Any user running chord commands with user-provided text.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `a-r` shortcut handles reason text containing apostrophes, double quotes, dollar signs, backticks, and other shell metacharacters without breaking.
2. The audit-set summary is correctly persisted with the full reason text, verbatim.
3. All other chord commands (a-y approve, producer review, update, search, note-edit, prompt) continue to handle valid input unchanged.
4. Regression tests verify shell metacharacter safety for user-provided shortcut values.
5. All existing herdr tests pass.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — `substituteIdentifiers` does raw replacement; needs shell-escaping
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `a-r` command template embeds `<reason>` in single quotes
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — form dialog dispatches the substituted command
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `buildRunInPaneArgs` / `run-in-pane.sh` execution path

## Constraints

- Fix must not change the `a-r` chord key binding or its visible behaviour (form dialog, pane, confirmation).
- The fix should be scoped to `substituteIdentifiers` in `form-dialog.ts`; avoid changes to `wl` CLI unless necessary.
- Must work cross-platform (Linux, macOS, Windows).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk**: Escaping strategy must cover all shell metacharacters (quotes, backticks, `$()`, `|`, `&`, `;`, `\`, newlines). **Mitigation**: use `printf '%q'` or equivalent well-tested escaping; test with comprehensive metacharacter set.
- **Risk**: Other shortcuts with user-provided identifiers (`<producer_comment>`, `<search_term>`, `<status>`, `<stage>`, `<title>`, `<description>`, `<prompt>`, `<note_text>`) likely share the same vulnerability. **Mitigation**: document as a follow-up; scope this item to `a-r` only.
- **Risk**: Changing the escaping strategy may require updating all shortcut templates to remove pre-existing quotes. **Mitigation**: if template changes are needed, apply consistently across all shortcuts in this item.
- **Risk**: Choosing a file-based approach (`--summary-file`) for `wl audit-set` adds complexity. **Mitigation**: prefer shell-escaping of the substituted value as the minimal fix; defer file-based approach to follow-up.
- **Risk**: `printf '%q'` output may differ between bash and zsh. **Mitigation**: test on the two most common shells; use `printf '%q'` which is POSIX-compatible in practice.
- **Assumption**: The `a-r` chord is the only shortcut currently reported as broken by metacharacters in user input.
- **Assumption**: `wl audit-set --summary` correctly accepts arbitrary text when properly quoted by the shell.
- **Scope-creep risk**: Fixing all shortcuts at once would be a larger feature. Record as a linked discovery item rather than expanding scope.

## Related work

- WL-0MP082Y1Q003GCUM — Audit internal shell command construction for proper escaping of user text (Worklog src/ only, not herdr)
- WL-0MOZUVGL6008QV45 — Prevent shell command substitution in wl audit text updates (added --audit-file, but herdr shortcut path still uses --summary in shell)
- WL-0MRSGMTYU009OZCF — Add --audit-file to wl audit-set (completed, but --summary-file not added)

- **WL-0MQOIBTHR002VMEK** – Add Guardrails to Protect Worklog Data Integrity (completed)
- **WL-0MQDUOK9K002QHJU** – Stage-based shortcut condition filters (completed)
- **WL-0MQDR5JBV0054CBY** – End-to-end test for detail view shortcut result handling (completed)

- `packages/herdr/README.md` — relevant to shell command execution and pane handling
- `CLI.md` — documents shortcut chords and `a-r` command
- `CHANGELOG.md` — tracks shortcut chord history

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The shell command fails to parse because the apostrophe in the reason text terminates the single-quoted string early. Source: user report. Final: confirmed.
- Q: "Is this the only shortcut affected by this class of bug?" — Answer: Not known yet; other shortcuts with user-provided identifiers (`<producer_comment>`, `<search_term>`, `<title>`, etc.) may have the same vulnerability but have not been reported. Source: code review. Final: likely, but scope this item to `a-r` only.

Source: prior work WL-0MOZUVGL6008QV45 established file-based handoff as the preferred long-term pattern; this item is scoped to the quickest path to fixing the reported bug. # Unify audit freshness: remove `isAuditNotReadyFresh` competing predicate

## Problem statement

The codebase defines audit freshness **twice**, with different semantics, so the
icon/dispatch paths and the ordering tier can disagree about whether the same
audit is fresh. `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` uses a one-sided time gate
(`auditedAt > updatedAt - AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`, 60 000 ms),
while `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `isAuditNotReadyFresh()` uses a strict
`auditedAt >= updatedAt` with no tolerance. WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE unified only the
icon and dispatch paths; the ordering path was left behind with a competing
predicate. Removing the competitor restores the single-source-of-truth guarantee
and makes all three consumers agree for every input.

## Users and user stories

- **Operator triaging the work queue** — As an operator, when I see the fresh
  audit icon on a work item, the ordering tier should treat that same item as
  audited-not-ready so it is boosted consistently; I should not see an item that
  is "fresh" in one view and "stale" in another.
- **Downtime dispatcher / agent** — As the audit-dispatch path, I rely on the
  single `isAuditFresh` predicate for re-dispatch decisions; no ordering tier
  should be able to contradict it.
- **Maintainer** — As a maintainer, I want exactly one place that decides audit
  timestamp freshness so future changes cannot silently diverge again.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Single freshness comparison.** `isAuditNotReadyFresh` in
   `packages/shared/src/database.ts` is removed, or delegates its timestamp
   comparison to the shared `isAuditFresh`
   (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`), retaining only its `readyToClose === false`
   and audit-presence gates. Verified by a repo search showing the only
   `auditedAt`-vs-`updatedAt` comparison is the shared helper (plus tests that
   intentionally assert it).
2. **Symmetric at-or-near semantics.** The freshness time gate treats an audit
   as fresh when `|auditedAt - updatedAt| < AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`
   (60 000 ms), replacing the current one-sided
   `auditedAt > updatedAt - tolerance`. Verification: unit tests cover inputs on
   both sides of the tolerance boundary.
3. **No re-implementation elsewhere.** No other file re-implements an
   `auditedAt` vs `updatedAt` comparison. Verification: repo search for
   `auditedAt`/`updatedAt` timestamp comparisons returns only the shared helper
   and its consuming call sites.
4. **Consumers agree.** Tests assert that the icon path
   (`auditIcon`/`stageDisplayIcon`), the downtime-dispatch path
   (`selectAuditCandidate`/`hasFreshAudit`), and the ordering path
   (`sortItemsByScore`/`computeScore`/`selectBySortIndex`) return the same
   freshness verdict for: fresh, stale, just-persisted (within tolerance), and
   missing-audit inputs.
5. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
   the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
6. **Full suite green.** The full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.

## Constraints

- **Fingerprint gate unchanged.** The primary content-fingerprint gate in
  `isAuditFresh` (stored fingerprint == current fingerprint ⇒ fresh) is the
  canonical behaviour and must not be altered; only the fallback time gate is
  affected by the symmetric-semantics change.

  and `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, storedFingerprint?, currentFingerprint?)`;
  the fallback time gate is `auditTime > updateTime - tolerance` (one-sided).
  Header comment claims this is the single source of truth (WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE).
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — private `isAuditNotReadyFresh(audit, itemUpdatedAt)`
  (≈ line 658) enforces `readyToClose === false` plus

  `Math.abs(auditTime - updateTime) < AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`
  (with the existing NaN guard and fail-closed behaviour).
- Remove `isAuditNotReadyFresh`, or reduce it to a thin wrapper that applies the
  `audit` presence + `readyToClose === false` gates and delegates the timestamp
  comparison to `isAuditFresh`, so the ordering tier, the icon path and the
  dispatch path share one definition.
- Update `sortItemsByScore`, `computeScore`, `compareAuditNotReadyTier` (and
  `selectBySortIndex`) to use the delegated predicate.
- Reconcile inline predicate copies in tests to the shared helper.
- Add agreement tests covering fresh / stale / just-persisted / missing-audit
  inputs across the three consumers.

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — Remove `isAuditNotReadyFresh` or delegate

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Dispatch freshness consumer; verify

- `packages/herdr/src/icons.test.ts` — Extend/add symmetric-boundary and

# Explicit child-audit coverage so covered children are not re-dispatched

## Problem statement

A `completed`/`in_review` child work item that is covered by a fresh parent
audit currently has no record of that coverage, so the worklist shows the plain
`in_review` stage icon (🔍) and the queue looks unaudited. We need an explicit,
derived notion of "covered by parent" that both the icon display and the audit
selection path can consume, without re-introducing redundant child-audit
dispatch.

## Users and user stories

- **Producer reviewing the release queue** — As a producer, when I look at a
  covered child under an audited parent, I want to see that it is covered
  (rather than a bare 🔍), so the queue accurately reflects audit state.
- **Operator triaging the work queue** — As an operator, I want the icon to be
  honest: covered children look covered, and genuinely uncovered children do not
  masquerade as audited.
- **Downtime dispatcher / agent** — As the audit-dispatch path, I must never
  spawn a redundant child audit, whether or not the child is covered.

## Discovery correction

The original description's premise that a covered child "is re-dispatched" is
**stale**: `WL-0MSTLFW14000KPEC` (completed, commit `5a20fa4c`) already added
`--root-only` to the audit-tier query in `getNextAuditCandidate`
(`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`), and `fetchReviewQueueState`
(`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) is root-only too, so **no child ever enters
the audit dispatch tier**. Today the only real gap is the *display/coverage*
gap; dispatch is already safe.

Current population: the root-only `completed`/`in_review` queue is empty, and
the only two `completed`/`in_review` children (`WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT`,
`WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5`) sit under a **demoted** parent (`WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2`,
`open`/`plan_complete`) with no fresh parent audit — i.e. they are genuinely
*uncovered*.

Producer decisions from the intake interview:

- **Coverage is derived at read time** (option 1a) — a child is covered iff its
  parent has a fresh audit; no persisted coverage reference and no schema
  migration.
- **Dispatch stays root-only** (option 2a) — never relax `--root-only`; an
  uncovered child is *flagged*, not dispatched.
- **Distinct greyed indicator** (option 3b) — covered children show the parent's
  audit symbol in a dimmed style, not the bright audit icon.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Coverage is derived, not persisted.** A child (`parentId` set) is treated
   as *covered* iff its direct parent has a fresh audit, determined by the single
   shared `isAuditFresh` predicate (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) over the
   parent's `auditedAt`/`updatedAt`/`fingerprint`/`currentFingerprint`. No new
   `audit_results` coverage column/row and no schema migration is introduced.
   Verification: unit test plus a repo check showing no new persisted coverage
   field and no competing freshness comparison (cf. `WL-0MUBVH7ZR009PP80`).
2. **Dispatch safety is preserved and tested.** `getNextAuditCandidate` continues
   to query `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json` and
   `selectAuditCandidate` never selects a child. Tests assert that neither a
   covered child nor an uncovered child is ever returned as an audit candidate
   (children are never dispatched independently — `WL-0MSTLFW14000KPEC`).
3. **Covered children display a distinct dimmed indicator.** For a
   `completed`/`in_review` child with no own audit but a fresh covering parent
   audit, `stageDisplayIcon` (and therefore the list prefix `getIconPrefix` and
   the metadata Stage row) renders the parent's audit-result symbol in a
   **dimmed/grey** style (visually distinct from the bright audit icon), and the
   metadata panel names the covering parent (e.g. `covered by <parent-id>`).
   Verification: icon/metadata unit tests asserting the dimmed glyph and the
   parent reference, and asserting the bright glyph is *not* used.
4. **Uncovered children are honest and undispatching.** A child with no own audit
   and no fresh parent audit shows the plain `in_review` stage icon (not the
   covered indicator) and is never added to the audit dispatch tier. Durable
   reporting of the uncovered population is delegated to
   `WL-0MUBVH9FV0027COG` (out of scope here). Verification: unit test covering a
   demoted/stale parent child.
5. **Tests cover the full matrix.** New/updated tests cover: (a) covered child →
   dimmed covered indicator, not dispatched; (b) uncovered child (parent
   demoted/stale) → plain stage icon, still not dispatched; (c) a parent audit
   that becomes stale → the previously covered child reverts to uncovered; (d) a
   child with its own fresh audit still shows its own audit result (unchanged).
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — in
   particular `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (child-verdict reuse / coverage) and the
   comments in `icons.ts`, `downtime-worker.ts` and `fetcher.ts`.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- No schema change / migration: coverage is derived (no `audit_results` coverage
  column, no sync-format change).
- Reuse the single shared `isAuditFresh` predicate; do **not** introduce a
  competing `auditedAt` vs `updatedAt` comparison.
- A child's own audit result always wins over inherited coverage.
- Keep the existing icon vocabulary; the covered indicator differs only by
  dimming/grey styling, not by a new glyph.
- No change to the audit skill's child-audit execution modes.
- Text-only (`noIcons`) mode must gain a `[BRACKET]`-style fallback for the
  covered indicator (e.g. `[COVERED]`) so it is never silently dropped.

## Existing state

- `getNextAuditCandidate` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts:888`) and
  `fetchReviewQueueState` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:713`) already use
  `--root-only`; `selectAuditCandidate`
  (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:6056`) filters `!isAuditFresh(...)`.
- `stageDisplayIcon` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts:340`) returns the plain stage
  icon when a `in_review` item has no/ stale audit; `getIconPrefix` and the
  metadata Stage row both consume it.
- The `WorkItem` model exposes `parentId`; the worklist nests children under
  expanded parents, so a child's parent audit state is available in the worklist
  layer.
- `AuditResult` (`packages/shared/src/types.ts`) has no coverage/parent
  reference; `audit_results.fingerprint` was added additively
  (`WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K`).
- `wl list --json` does not expose `currentFingerprint`, so list-rendering
  freshness degrades to the 60 s time gate unless the worklist computes it.

## Desired change

Add derived coverage to the display path (and only the display path):

- Enrich each `completed`/`in_review` child item in the worklist render model
  with its parent's audit state (or a computed `coveredByParent` flag), computed
  via the shared `isAuditFresh` predicate.
- Return the parent's audit-result symbol from `stageDisplayIcon` (or a new
  unambiguous helper) for covered children, and render it **dimmed** in the list
  row and metadata panel; add a `covered by <parent-id>` metadata row.
- Leave the audit dispatch query root-only; add regression tests that children
  are never candidates.
- Document the derived-coverage semantics in the audit skill.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `stageDisplayIcon`: covered-child branch /
  optional parent-audit inputs; reuse `isAuditFresh` unchanged.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `renderRow` / `getIconPrefix` dimming of the
  covered indicator; `buildMetaRows` `covered by <parent-id>` row.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — enrich child items with parent audit state
  when nesting; comments noting root-only is preserved.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — comments on coverage vs root-only
  dispatch (selection logic unchanged).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — comment on root-only + coverage; regression
  tests.
- Tests: `packages/shared/src/icons.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist-*.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-review-queue.test.ts`.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — document derived child coverage.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — ANSI leaks into shared icon helpers.** Applying dim in the
  dependency-free `icons.ts` could corrupt display-width maths. Mitigation:
  `icons.ts` returns the plain glyph; the worklist renderer applies `ANSI.dim`
  around the covered indicator only.
- **Risk — fingerprint degradation.** `wl list --json` lacks
  `currentFingerprint`, so list-rendering coverage falls back to the 60 s time
  gate. Mitigation: use the worklist's already-computed current fingerprint where
  available and document the degradation (same semantics as the audit tier).
- **Risk — noIcons / narrow terminals.** A dimmed glyph with no text fallback
  would disappear in `noIcons` mode. Mitigation: add a `[COVERED]` fallback and
  keep the metadata row as the textual source of truth.
- **Risk — scope creep into the gate/doctor work.** Reporting the uncovered
  population belongs to `WL-0MUBVH9FV0027COG`; record any new opportunities as
  linked work items, not scope here.
- **Assumption — direct parent only (depth 1).** Transitive/grandchild coverage
  is out of scope unless the producer says otherwise.
- **Assumption — own audit wins.** A child with its own fresh audit is rendered
  exactly as today.
- **Assumption — coverage is display/selection-only.** No persisted state, hence
  no sync-related timestamp churn.
- **Assumption — the detail (metadata) view may not have the parent loaded.** When
  parent audit state is unavailable there, the `covered by` row is omitted rather
  than guessed; the list view (where the parent is in hand) is authoritative.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSTLFW14000KPEC` (completed) — Exclude child items from audit-tier
  dispatch selection (`--root-only`, commit `5a20fa4c`).
- `WL-0MUBVH9FV0027COG` (open) — Gate leak: completed/in_review items with no
  audit (flag + doctor report); owns durable uncovered reporting.
- `WL-0MUBVH7ZR009PP80` (open) — Unify audit freshness: remove
  `isAuditNotReadyFresh` competing predicate.
- `WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE` (completed) — Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic
  across icon display and downtime dispatcher (source of this discovery).
- `WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K` (completed) — Audit freshness: content-fingerprint gate
  as primary.
- `WL-0MU2QKB98007BKYT` (completed) — Re-sort no longer invalidates previously
  fresh audits via `updatedAt` churn.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1: How should a child's audit coverage be expressed?** (a) derived at read
  time; (b) recorded inherited reference; (c) every child gets its own verdict.
  **Answer (producer): (a) derived at read time.** No schema change, no write
  churn. Source: interactive intake reply.
- **Q2: Given `--root-only` already excludes all children from audit dispatch,
  what should AC5 ("uncovered child still dispatched") become?** (a) keep
  children fully excluded, flag uncovered only; (b) relax root-only for uncovered
  children; (c) retire the dispatch assertions. **Answer (producer): (a) keep
  children fully excluded from dispatch; flag uncovered via icon, defer durable
  reporting to `WL-0MUBVH9FV0027COG`.** Source: interactive intake reply.
- **Q3: What should the queue icon show for a covered child?** (a) reuse the
  parent's audit-result icon; (b) a distinct "covered by parent" indicator;
  (c) no change. **Answer (producer): (b) a distinct indicator — preferably the
  same symbols rendered in grey.** Source: interactive intake reply. Research:
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` exposes `ANSI.dim` (`\x1b[2m`), so a grey
  variant of the existing audit glyphs is feasible without new glyphs.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** – Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit (completed)
- **WL-0MR983JD2001149O** – Clean up duplicate child WL-0MR89RUU1007L0U1 (completed)

# Measure the post-change benefit of mode-aware AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM

## Problem statement

WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME makes the downtime dispatcher pass a mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` to dispatched audit panes: `2` in cheap mode when a second local slot is genuinely free and the dispatch is single-flight, `1` otherwise. The wiring is live in the running `dev` build (herdr `dist/` rebuilt 2026-09-24 18:38; running checkout HEAD `e1bea036` includes `6188a90d`) — **no `dev`→`main` release is required** for it to take effect on this machine.

The benefit has not been observed yet. The first post-change cheap window (2026-09-25 01:00-10:00) contained no dispatched audits, so the audit-only `PARALLELISM=2` path was never exercised.

This item is the operational follow-up: capture a measurement that actually exercises the path.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants to confirm the change raises cheap-window local slot utilisation without increasing remote fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-change proxy usage report covering at least one 01:00-10:00 cheap window recorded, and a dispatched audit within that window shown to overlap its Phase 2 children with the parent (peak cheap-mode concurrency 2, not 1).
2. Cheap-window local utilisation compared against the immediate pre-change cheap windows and the 2026-08-22_3 reference, and reported (up, flat, or down). Utilisation is measured by **avg concurrency (while busy) = total compute ÷ busy time** and/or **slot utilisation = total compute ÷ (window × slots)**, not by busy % (which saturates at one busy slot).
3. Remote fallback rate compared against the pre-change rate and reported (must not increase).

# Interview: LLM-Assisted Question Extraction

**Headline:** When `wl interview <id>` finds no parseable questions using the deterministic parser, optionally invoke a local LLM (via the existing embedding infrastructure) to extract unanswered questions from the description in free text.

## Problem Statement

The deterministic parser (`extractClarifyingSection` + `parseQAPairs`) requires an exact section header and rigid formatting. Real work items use varied formats (e.g., `## Appendix: Clarifying questions \& answers` with `- **Q1**: "..." — Answer (user@...): "..."). As a result, zero of the 17 `needsProducerReview=true` items are currently detectable. The original audit rejected WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 stating: "The command does not reliably detect questions."

An LLM normaliser turns this hard format dependency into a soft one — it can extract questions regardless of prose format.

## Users

- **Producers** running `wl interview <id>` — they want the command to find questions even when the description doesn't follow the canonical format.
- **Developers** — they want the feature to work with local models (Ollama/Foundry), not require a cloud API key.

**User Story:** "As a producer running `wl interview`, I want the system to find questions even when they're written in natural prose, so I can answer them without manually searching the description."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the deterministic parser finds no questions, and the `--llm` flag is set (or `intelligent: true` in config), the command calls a local LLM via the existing OpenAI-compatible embedding infrastructure `src/lib/search.ts`.
2. The LLM is asked to return a JSON array of `{ question: string }` objects extracted from the description, or an empty array if none found.
3. Each extracted question is presented to the user interactively (same `createPromptLoop` readline flow) for confirmation and answer.
4. Only confirmed questions are written to the description using the **deterministic re-serialiser** (`rebuildQAPairs` / `rebuildDescription`) — never written directly from LLM output.
5. When no LLM is available (no config, network failure, timeout), the command falls back to the existing deterministic-only message with no error.
6. The LLM call is bounded: description is truncated to 8 KB, a timeout of 15 seconds is enforced.
7. Tests cover: mock client returns valid questions, mock returns empty, mock throws error, no config available, timeout.

## Configuration

Opt-in via one of:
- `--llm` CLI flag: `wl interview <id> --llm`
- Config file: `intelligent: true` under `interview` section in `.worklog/config.yaml`

## Constraints

- No new dependencies — reuse `src/lib/search.ts` embedding infrastructure (OpenAI-compatible client, config resolution, graceful degradation).
- LLM is a *text completion* client, not an embedding client — but the same provider config, base URL, model, and auth apply. We should either:
  - (a) Add a `llm.*` config section parallel to `embedding.*`
  - (b) Or reuse the same provider config (the embedder already supports any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
- The deterministic parser remains the primary path; LLM is strictly a fallback.
- Output is interactive-only (no --json mode for LLM calls).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — New `--llm` option, LLM client invocation, user confirmation loop for extracted questions.
- `src/cli-types.ts` — Add `llm?: boolean` to `InterviewOptions`.
- `src/lib/search.ts` — Potentially add a `ChatClient` class alongside the existing `OpenAIEmbedder`, or reuse its config resolution for a completion client.
- `src/config.ts` — Add `interview.llm` or `llm.*` config schema.
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — New test cases for LLM path.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Model availability:** Not all setups have an LLM configured. Fallback must be silent and graceful.
- **Cost:** One completion call per invocation (~2-3 KB input) is cheap even at $0.001/call, but should be bounded.
- **Hallucination:** The mandatory user-confirmation step before writing to the description mitigates this.
- **Scope creep risk:** Users may want batch extraction across multiple items or LLM-generated answers. Track separately.

# Bug — Stage filters hide in-progress items

## Problem

Stage-filtered worklist views (`/wl plan`, `/wl plan_complete`, `/wl intake`, `/wl intake_complete`) run `fetchItemsByStage()` which issues `wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only`. Per **AC2 of WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G** (confirmed by operator in the brief's Appendix Q2), the "open" status filter explicitly excludes items with `status=blocked`, `status=in-progress`, or `status=completed`.

Before the `in_progress` stage was retired, this was harmless: actively-worked items sat in `stage=in_progress` and the rule only excluded from other stage lists. After **WL-0MTOHS5B4001Y9FX** ("Remove the in_progress stage"), an actively-worked item retains its pipeline stage (`plan_complete` or `intake_complete`) and only flips `status` to `in-progress`. The exclusion now makes actively-worked items **invisible** in the stage filter that corresponds to their pipeline position.

## Concrete example

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | **WL-0MSZVB902004AZZN** ("Pre-fill vs working in Web UI") |
| stage | `plan_complete` |
| status | `in-progress` |
| assignee | Map |

This item is actively being implemented by the herdr downtime worker (agent "Map"). It is **not visible** when a user filters by `plan`/`plan_complete` in the herdr worklist, even though it belongs in that stage. The user sees 0 items belonging to the item's stage while work is underway.

## Root cause

`fetcher.ts` `STAGE_STATUS` defaults every stage to `status=open` with a single-stage exception for `in_review` (fixed in **WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW**). No exception exists for stages where claimed work is possible (`plan_complete`, `intake_complete`).

The dispatcher's safety guarantee (prevent re-dispatch of claimed work) comes from the **CAS claim** (`wl update --status in-progress --if-status ...`), not from UI-level exclusion. The UI exclusion provides protection but at the cost of making actively-worked items invisible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Filtering by `plan_complete` in the herdr worklist shows all items in that stage, including those with `status=in-progress`.
2. Filtering by `intake_complete` in the herdr worklist shows all items in that stage, including those with `status=in-progress`.
3. The `fetchItemsByStage()` function applies `--status open,in-progress` for stages that can hold claimed work (`plan_complete`, `intake_complete`), and `--status open` only for stages that cannot (`idea`, `completed`, `done`).
4. The existing `in_review` exception (`completed,in-progress,open`) is preserved and verified by tests.
5. A unit test asserts the correct `--status` argument per stage, including `in-progress` for `plan_complete` and `intake_complete`.
6. No regression: items with `status=blocked` or `status=completed` remain excluded from non-review stages.
7. The Pi TUI worklist stage filter follows the same pattern (both CLI and DB paths in `tools.ts`).

## Design decisions considered

1. **Per-stage exception list (preferred)**: `STAGE_STATUS` maps each stage to its allowed status set. This is the same approach used for `in_review` in WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW but applied systematically.
2. **`--status open,in-progress` for all stages except completed/done**: Simpler but would surface items with `status=in-progress` in the `idea` stage (should not happen but protects against data corruption).
3. **Remove status filter from stage filter entirely**: Would show `blocked` and `completed` items too, which is worse UX.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G** — "When filtering by stage, show all open work items in that stage" (origin of the `status=open` rule)
- **WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW** — "Herdr: in_review stage filter shows 0 items" (same failure class, fixed only for `in_review`)
- **WL-0MTOHS5B4001Y9FX** — "Remove the in_progress stage" (created the conditions for this bug)
- **WL-0MSZVB902004AZZN** — "Pre-fill vs working in Web UI" (concrete example of the bug in action)

## Key files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `STAGE_STATUS`, `fetchItemsByStage()`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/tools.ts` — `createListWorkItemsWithStage`, `createListWorkItemsWithStageDb` (must stay in sync)
- Test files: `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` (fetcher tests), TUI extension tests

## Goal

As a pi extension maintainer, I need the Worklog recovery extension to stop crashing the pi process when its captured `ExtensionContext` becomes stale after a session replacement/reload, so headless/audit pi runs are not aborted with a spurious `Connection error.`

## Problem

`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` captures the handler `ctx` in a module-level notify closure:

```ts
let _notifyFn: ((message: string, level: 'info' | 'warning' | 'error') => void) | null = null;
pi.on('agent_end', async (_event, ctx) => {
  _notifyFn = (message, level) => ctx.ui.notify(message, level);
});
pi.on('turn_end', async (_event, ctx) => {
  if (!_notifyFn) _notifyFn = (message, level) => ctx.ui.notify(message, level);
});
```

(and again around line ~212). `_notifyFn` is later invoked asynchronously from the recovery retry loop
(`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`, called by `triggerInvisibleContinue`). After pi replaces or reloads the
session, `ctx.ui` throws:

```
Error: This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload. Do not use a captured pi or command ctx after ctx.newSession(), ctx.fork(), ctx.switchSession(), or ctx.reload(). ...
```

Because the call originates in a timer/async callback (`process.processTicksAndRejections`), pi does not catch it,
the Node process exits (stderr ends with the `Node.js v22.22.1` crash banner), and the calling consumer (e.g. the
SorraAgents audit runner) surfaces `provider_error: Connection error.`

## Evidence

- Stack trace: `at _notifyFn (register-recovery.ts:71:41)` → `at _notifyRetryAttempt (register-recovery.ts:549:5)` → `at triggerInvisibleContinue (register-recovery.ts:391:7)` → `at process.processTicksAndRejections`.
- Captured in SorraAgents audit debug log `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB.jsonl` (`context=parent`, `reason=provider_error`, `elapsed_seconds≈713`), and in every non-empty `raw_stderr` `provider_error` entry across that corpus.
- Originating SorraAgents item: **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F** (this is the handoff requested there; the SorraAgents side will make its own `pi-client` extensions stale-ctx-safe and track its audit-runner change separately).

## Desired change

`_notifyFn` must never throw after the ctx is invalidated. Re-bind/re-capture the notify function from the
current handler ctx on each event (and/or guard the call), so a stale ctx results in the notification being
skipped rather than an uncaught exception. Do not change retry semantics otherwise.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The stale-ctx uncaught exception no longer occurs: the retry notification path (`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`)
   never throws when the session ctx has been replaced/reloaded; the notification is skipped when the ctx is stale.
2. Regression test added: invoking the retry notification path with an invalidated/stale ctx asserts no throw.
3. The Worklog extension test suite passes with the change.
4. All related documentation and code comments are updated, including the recovery module header.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — `_notifyFn` capture and call sites.

## Related work

- SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F (SorraAgents) — corrected root-cause analysis and handoff.
- WL-0MQZX8BTN006N4BF — Automatically recover from appropriate server errors (parent retry-loop context).

# Downtime audits: prevent host-wide audit-slot / Local Proxy saturation from failing concurrent audits

**discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 (SorraAgents worklog)

## Summary

On 2026-09-26 at least four downtime-dispatched audits were running concurrently on this
host, saturating both the shared Local Proxy and the audit runner's **host-wide** audit slot
(cheap-proxy mode forces `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`). As a result the audit for
`SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` failed on **every** Pi call and was aborted with no verdict:

```
Audit concurrency limit reached: audit concurrency queue 'audit' saturated:
no slot within 90s (waited 90.1s, 1 item(s) in queue)
```

Supporting observations at the time:

- A direct Local Proxy generation request (`POST http://192.168.0.199:8000/v1/chat/completions`,
  model `plan`) returned no response within 180s, while `/v1/models` answered immediately.
- Host load average was ~70.
- Concurrent audits: `SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD` (SorraAgents), `SA-0MTTSWHQE0072N9J` (SorraAgents),
  `CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0` (ContextHub) alongside the aborted `SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63`.
- The failure degraded every acceptance criterion to `partial` on infrastructure evidence
  (not a code assessment), so the audit produced no usable verdict.

## Existing coverage that did not prevent this

- **Per-instance active-audit detection** (`WL-0MT47BQAT00375VB`, tests `WL-0MT47BMR7003ZQ66`):
  the audit tier is skipped when a non-stale `kind=audit` dispatch marker in
  `<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` maps to an item still `in_progress`.
- **Proxy-slot gating** already exists in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
  (`slots_stale`, free-slot counts, local lease).

The observed concurrency spanned **multiple projects and possibly multiple herdr instances**,
and the audit runner's own host-wide semaphore/queue is a separate mechanism from the
dispatcher's per-project slot gate. The gap (per-instance vs host-wide coordination, and the
audit runner's 90s admission bound turning contention into an infra-partial verdict) is the
subject of this item.

## Desired change

1. **Host-wide audit serialisation (or deferral).** At most one audit-tier `/skill:audit` run
   should be actively executing per host — across herdr instances and projects — **or** the
   dispatcher must skip/defer audit dispatch while the audit runner's host-wide slot/queue is
   occupied or while the Local Proxy reports no free slots.
2. **Tolerate contention instead of failing.** When saturation is transient, the audit runner's
   admission wait should be sized so the run waits for a slot (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`) and/or the
   dispatch is retried later, rather than aborting with an infra-partial verdict. An audit must
   not be reported as unavailable merely because other audits are legitimately running.
3. **Regression test.** With a simulated occupied host-wide audit slot (or two dispatcher
   instances on one host), a second audit is not started; the candidate falls through to the
   next tier or is deferred.
4. **Observability.** Log a clear skip/defer reason (e.g. `audit-host-saturated`) that includes
   the number of concurrent audits and the audit-runner queue/slot state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Audit dispatch is serialised host-wide (single active audit run per host) **or** audit
      dispatch is skipped/deferred when the host-wide audit slot or Local Proxy slots are
      unavailable, including across projects and herdr instances.
- [ ] A regression test proves a second concurrent audit is not started while one is active
      (simulated occupied slot / second instance), and that the candidate is deferred or falls
      through to another tier.
- [ ] Contention produces a clear `audit-host-saturated` (or equivalent) skip/defer log line
      with the concurrent-audit count and queue/slot state.
- [ ] Documentation of the host-wide coordination contract and its relationship to the existing
      per-instance active-audit detection and proxy-slot gating.

## Evidence

- Aborted audit log (SorraAgents):
  `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_run_SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63_20260926T175346.log`
- SorraAgents work item with the full write-up and the producer Q&A: `SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63`.

## Related

- `WL-0MSI9WPNI0044RL8` — Audit dispatch tier
- `WL-0MT47BQAT00375VB` — Active-audit detection & audit-tier skip
- `WL-0MT47BMR7003ZQ66` — Active-audit single-flight tests
- `WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY` — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions

## Notes

SorraAgents work items live in a separate worklog; this item is intentionally created in
ContextHub because the downtime dispatcher is implemented in `packages/herdr/`.

# Investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not closed on completion

## Problem statement

Pi agent sessions launched in Herdr panes run `pi` in **interactive** mode with
an initial prompt (`packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`). When a skill
completes it emits a `</end_session>` marker, but nothing consumes that marker:
the interactive REPL simply waits for the next input, so the pane and its
~200 MB pi process stay alive forever. Over hours these abandoned sessions
accumulate — the operator observed **50 concurrent pi sessions / ~12.4 GB RSS
with ages up to 18+ hours**, contributing to severe CPU oversubscription
(load ~3× cores). Nothing transitions the session to a closed state on skill
completion, and there is no lifecycle hook that reaps sessions whose agent died
without emitting the marker.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — wants completed agent panes to disappear on their
  own so the machine is not oversubscribed and panes do not need manual pruning.
- **Downtime dispatcher** — spawns intake/plan/audit/risk-effort panes for every
  dispatched item; if those panes never close, the dispatcher floods the host.
- **Agents** — need their session to end cleanly (lease released, pane torn
  down) once their task and report are complete, without an operator click.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, when a dispatched `/skill:intake` or `/skill:plan` session
  finishes and writes its `</end_session>` report, I want the pane to close
  automatically so idle sessions do not accumulate.
- As a producer, I want an agent that stops to ask me a question (no
  `</end_session>`) to keep its pane open so I can answer it, but an agent whose
  process died silently to be cleaned up.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — graceful auto-close on completion.** When a session's final
   assistant message's concatenated text, `.rstrip()`-ed, ends with
   `</end_session>`, the pane is closed programmatically by the shared closure
   script so the process exits, the pane is torn down, and the proxy model
   lease is released — with no operator action. (Mechanism revised in planning:
   an in-process `agent_end`/`agent_settled` hook is NOT used, because the SDK
   exposes no `agent_settled` event and `agent_end` proved unreliable; the
   scheduled closure script owns this — see Appendix Q5.) Metric: a unit test
   with a fixture session whose last assistant text ends with the marker asserts
   a close is requested exactly once; an end-to-end check shows the pane closes
   within one reaper interval.
2. **AC2 — no false positives.** No close is requested when the final
   assistant message does not end with the marker — including a `</end_session>`
   quoted mid-message, a question-ended session, an aborted run, and a run that
   ended in a non-retryable error. Metric: negative-path unit tests for each
   case assert zero close requests, and an item with
   `needsProducerReview=true` is never auto-closed.
3. **AC3 — marker-less sessions are reaped (fail-closed).** Sessions whose agent
   died or was killed without emitting the marker do not linger indefinitely: a
   liveness/idle reaper closes panes whose agent process is gone or idle beyond
   a configurable threshold (default 30 minutes, per producer decision), while **never**
   closing a pane that is actively working, has live child processes, or has
   `needsProducerReview=true`. Metric: table-driven classifier tests plus an
   integration check on a synthetic abandoned pane.
4. **AC4 — `implement` panes remain excluded** from automatic close, preserving
   the AC6 precedent of `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN` unless the producer explicitly
   changes the policy. Metric: a test asserts an `implement` pane is never
   auto-closed.
5. **AC5 — child processes are not orphaned.** When a session exits or is
   terminated, its spawned children (e.g. audit/plan runners) are terminated
   with it, so none are reparented to PID 1. Metric: an integration test spawns
   a long-running child in a session-scoped process group, terminates the
   session, and asserts the child does not survive.
6. **AC6 — one shared idle/completion classifier.** The automatic hook and the
   `pane-triage` skill (`WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`) consume a single
   marker-detection + liveness helper, so the two mechanisms cannot diverge.
   Metric: both call the shared module; its classifier is covered by
   table-driven tests (marker at end accepted; marker mid-message rejected).
7. **AC7 — tests and documentation.** Unit and integration tests are added for
   every path. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
   including code comments, `packages/tui/extensions/README.md`, and any
   relevant `docs/` entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.

## Constraints

- Must not close a pane that is actively working **or** awaiting a producer
  answer.
- Mechanism (revised in planning): closure is performed by a scheduled,
  out-of-process closure script that reads session logs — NOT by an in-process
  `agent_end` hook. The script must never race the existing `agent_end`
  recovery/compaction flow: it only closes a pane whose session is demonstrably
  settled (idle beyond the threshold, or its agent process is gone).
- The existing downtime auto-close logic (`pane-lifecycle.ts`,
  `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN`) must remain intact and must not double-handle or race
  the new closure script; both must be idempotent.
- Auto-close must be configurable/overridable (threshold, on/off) so an operator
  can disable it without editing code.
- Headless modes (JSON/RPC) must be unaffected; gate UI-facing behaviour to TUI
  mode as `herdr-agent-state.ts` already does.
- Never close the invoking/current operator pane.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh` runs `pi` (interactive) with an
  initial prompt; on `pi` exit its `EXIT` trap calls
  `release-lease-on-exit.mjs` and Herdr tears the pane down when the primary
  process exits. **The gap is that `pi` never exits.**
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/` is the auto-loaded pi extension
  (`index.ts` wires activity indicator, model display, session health,
  guardrails, skill-path, recovery, lease release). It hooks `agent_end`,
  `session_shutdown`, `agent_start` and `turn_end`. Note: the pi SDK exposes
  **no** `agent_settled` event (verified against
  `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` `ExtensionAPI` types), so an
  `agent_settled`-based hook is not implementable as originally drafted.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` inspects
  the last assistant message on `agent_end` — a precedent for reading final
  output, and a coordination point so recovery finishes before shutdown.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` classifies **dispatched** panes by
  worklog stage and closes everything except `implement`; it only covers panes
  recorded in `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, so manually opened and
  marker-less panes are never reaped.
- `~/.pi/agent/extensions/herdr-agent-state.ts` reports `idle`/`working`/
  `blocked` to Herdr but never closes anything.
- The report helper (`~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py`)
  appends the canonical `</end_session>` marker and is emitted by every skill's
  end-of-session report.
- Observed evidence: 44–50 live `pi` processes (~200 MB RSS each), sessions with
  completed work still alive, and orphaned `audit_runner` children reparented to
  PID 1.

## Desired change

Build an out-of-process, script-driven session-closure capability (revised in
planning — see Appendix Q5):

1. A **shared closure classifier** (pure logic, table-driven tests) that
   decides, for one session/pane: idle-with-marker, idle-without-marker
   (agent process gone or idle beyond the 30-minute threshold), active, or
   never-close (`implement`, `needsProducerReview=true`, invoking pane).
2. A **closure script** (CLI) that scans herdr panes, classifies each via the
   shared classifier, and closes eligible panes idempotently, writing a ledger.
   This is the programmatic handler; it does not depend on the unreliable
   in-process `agent_end` event.
3. The script is **scheduled** to run periodically (herdr downtime-worker tick
   or equivalent) with on/off + threshold configuration, and is idempotent
   against the existing `pane-lifecycle.ts` dispatch monitor.
4. Session-scoped child processes are terminated on closure so none are
   orphaned to PID 1.
5. The **`pane-triage` skill** (`WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`) reuses the same
   classifier/script rather than re-deriving idle state from the session log
   (coordination: comment + dependency edge).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts` — **new**: shared closure classifier (marker detection + liveness + close eligibility). Pure, no I/O.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.test.ts` — **new**: table-driven classifier tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts` — **new**: closure script orchestration (scan → classify → close → ledger), injectable I/O.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.test.ts` — **new**: fixture-based reaper tests (exclusions, idempotence, no-op).
- `packages/herdr/src/process-group.ts` + `.test.ts` — **new**: session-scoped child-process teardown.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — existing dispatch-pane classifier; keep intact, de-duplicate against the new closure script.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — periodic wiring/scheduling of the closure script.
- `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh` — reference only (exit/lease-release path).
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — document the closure script and its configuration.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py` — reference only (marker source).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `</end_session>` is the single canonical terminal signal and
  is always the final line of a completed skill report.
- **Risk — premature close.** An in-process `agent_end` hook could race
  recovery/compaction. Mitigated by the planning decision to close
  out-of-process from a scheduled script that requires the session to be
  settled (agent process gone, or idle beyond the 30-minute threshold).
- **Risk — false-positive close** of an interactive session mid-conversation;
  mitigated by strict final-message marker matching plus negative-path tests.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Orphaned-child reaping and the marker-less reaper
  overlap existing work; if either grows large it should become a child item
  rather than inflate this fix.
- **Risk — double handling.** The downtime `pane-lifecycle` monitor may race
  the new closure script; both must be idempotent and the winner must be
  deterministic.
- **Risk — marker-less session misclassification.** A genuinely working agent
  that is silent for >30 minutes could be reaped. Mitigated by requiring the
  agent process to be gone OR the idle threshold to be exceeded, plus
  live-child-process and `needsProducerReview` guards.

## Related work

- `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM` — Create pane-triage skill: gated close of idle panes (manual complement; reuses the shared classifier/script — see Appendix Q1/Q5).
- `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN` — Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement (precedent; `implement` exception).
- `WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN` — Implement auto-close logic with implement exception.
- `WL-0MSGI7UIH008USVB` — Herdr plugin: release the Local Proxy model lease when a pi session is closed (exit/release path).
- `WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ` — Create a machine-hygiene skill that evaluates performance pressure (orphaned audit_runners, stale servers).
- `WL-0MSB19J56006E87J` — Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM).
- `WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO` — Fix orphaned ContextHub node processes that never exit after worktree cleanup.
- `WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O` — Auto-continue after mid-session compaction (session lifecycle precedent).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Deferral to the pane-triage skill (`WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`).**
  Should this item defer to pane-triage, or own the automatic lifecycle fix?
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-27):** Keep both. This item owns the automatic
  fix; pane-triage remains the approval-gated manual complement. Rationale:
  pane-triage's idle test is the same `</end_session>` marker and it never
  closes anything unattended, so it cannot prevent accumulation (50
  sessions/18h accumulated despite the operator being available), and it is
  blind to sessions whose agent died without emitting the marker. **Final:
  no deferral.** The producer further directed that a *script* perform the
  programmatic closure and that pane-triage reuse that script so the two
  cannot diverge (see Q5). This supersedes the earlier OPEN QUESTION.
- **Q2 — Marker-less / crashed sessions.**
  Is a gated manual close sufficient, or is an automatic liveness/idle reaper
  required? **Answer (producer):** automatic, fail-closed reaper is required
  (AC3), because marker-less sessions are invisible to pane-triage and
  dominated the observed backlog. **Final: automatic reaper.**
- **Q3 — Orphaned child-process cleanup (AC5) scope.**
  In scope here or a separate child item? **Answer (producer):** focus here —
  AC5 stays in this item (not split out). **Final: in scope.**
- **Q5 — Closure mechanism (in-process hook vs out-of-process script).**
  `agent_end` was found unreliable and the SDK exposes no `agent_settled`
  event. **Answer (producer):** do not rely on `agent_end`; write a script
  that programmatically handles the closures, and coordinate with
  `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM` so the pane-triage skill uses the script. **Final:
  out-of-process, scheduled closure script + shared classifier.**
- **Q6 — Idle threshold for the marker-less reaper.** **Answer (producer):**
  30 minutes. **Final: default 30 minutes, configurable.**
- **Q7 — Placement of the shared script.** **Open (assumption).**
  Recommended: ContextHub `packages/herdr/` (the pure classifier, CLI and
  scheduler live beside the existing `pane-lifecycle.ts`, and herdr's build
  and tests already cover them); the pane-triage skill (SorraAgents
  `skill/pane-triage/`) invokes the script. Alternative: place the CLI inside
  `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/scripts/` (crosses repos). Recorded as an
  assumption to validate at implementation.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-09-27** — Initial decomposition. Revised AC1/AC2/AC3 and the
  mechanism from an in-process `agent_end` hook to a scheduled, out-of-process
  closure script + shared classifier (producer decision, Appendix Q5/Q6);
  resolved Appendix Q1–Q3; split work into test-first child items. Session:
  see session-logging comment.
- **Q4 — Does `</end_session>` align with the session-close lifecycle?**
  **Answer (agent research):** Partially. It is the correct primary signal for
  graceful completions, but the pane-triage model misses sessions that died
  without emitting it. Evidence: live idle `pi` REPLs with completed work, plus
  `audit_runner` children reparented to PID 1 (parent died, no marker).
  Source: process inspection, `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/*`,
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py`.

## Purpose
A repeatable, safe diagnostic-and-remediation skill for hosts running many concurrent pi agent sessions and test suites. It must NEVER act autonomously without explicit producer approval.

## Required workflow (must be encoded in the skill)
1. **Evaluate** — collect performance metrics (load average, /proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}, free/swap, process & thread counts, per-command aggregate RSS, runnable count, stale devices) and render a before table with status symbols: low / warning / critical.

# CLI: treat `--parent null` as detach instead of creating a bogus `WL-NULL` parent

**As a** CLI/TUI user managing work-item hierarchy, **I want** `--parent null` to detach an item (set `parentId` to `null`), **so that** detaching a work item is discoverable and does not silently corrupt the hierarchy with an invalid parent reference.

## Problem

`normalizeCliId()` (`src/cli-utils.ts`) turns any bare token into `<PREFIX>-<TOKEN>`:

```ts
if (trimmed.includes('-')) return trimmed.toUpperCase();
return `${prefix}-${trimmed.toUpperCase()}`;
```

So `wl update <id> --parent null` produces the literal parent id **`WL-NULL`**, which does not exist. The item ends up with a dangling parent link rather than becoming top-level. The only working detach syntax today is the undocumented `--parent ""`.

### Evidence

- Reproduced live during the v1.0.16 release follow-up: `wl update WL-0MTF5WNZV003JKMJ --parent null` set `parentId = "WL-NULL"` (fixed with `--parent ""`).
- Two pre-existing items still carry the artefact: **WL-0MLGTKNKF14R37IA** and **WL-0MLGTKO880HYPZ2R** (both `done`, `parentId = "WL-NULL"`).
- `wl show WL-NULL` → "Work item not found".

## Desired behaviour

1. `wl update <id> --parent null` (case-insensitive) detaches the item: `parentId` becomes `null`, exit code 0, no `WL-NULL` written.
2. The same sentinel is accepted by `wl create` (`--parent null` == top-level item, the default).
3. Existing detach syntax `--parent ""` continues to work unchanged (backwards compatible).
4. A genuinely invalid parent id (e.g. a non-existent `WL-XXXX`) still fails as today — no behaviour change there.
5. `--parent` help text documents the detach form; `CLI.md` and `EXAMPLES.md` document it.
6. `wl doctor` detects dangling `WL-NULL` (or any non-existent) parent references and proposes a fix; the two known items are remediated.

## Suggested implementation

- Add a small `normalizeParentId(value, prefix)` helper (in `src/cli-utils.ts`) that maps case-insensitive `null` / `none` / `nil` / `-` (and empty string) to `null`, otherwise delegates to `normalizeCliId()`.
- Use it at both call sites: `src/commands/update.ts` (`parentCandidate`, ~L163) and `src/commands/create.ts` (`parentId`, ~L198).
- Keep `normalizeCliId()` unchanged so other id fields are unaffected.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `wl update <id> --parent null --json` sets `parentId: null`; `wl show <id> --json` confirms; no item is created or referenced as `WL-NULL`.
2. `wl create --title "x" --parent null --json` creates a top-level item (`parentId: null`).
3. `wl update <id> --parent ""` and `--parent none` both detach (documented aliases).
4. `wl update <id> --parent WL-DOESNOTEXIST` still errors (unchanged).
5. Unit tests for the new helper cover `null`, `NULL`, `none`, `-`, `""`, and a real/partial id.
6. CLI integration tests cover update-detach and create-top-level via `--parent null`.
7. `--parent` help text and `CLI.md`/`EXAMPLES.md` document detach.
8. `wl doctor` flags existing `WL-NULL` parent references; WL-0MLGTKNKF14R37IA and WL-0MLGTKO880HYPZ2R are cleaned to `parentId: null`.
9. `npm run build` and the full suite pass (build → test → commit order).

## Key files

- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `normalizeCliId`; add `normalizeParentId`
- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--parent` handling (~L163)
- `src/commands/create.ts` — `--parent` handling (~L198)
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — dangling-parent check
- `tests/unit/cli-args.test.ts` (or equivalent) — helper unit tests
- `tests/cli/` — update/create integration tests
- `CLI.md`, `EXAMPLES.md`

## Notes

- Discovered during the ContextHub v1.0.16 release follow-up (WL-0MUJKVZTZ003FX8S); the same `--parent null` mistake was made while detaching the four hydrator follow-ups.
- `--parent null` for `wl list` / `wl search` (filter for root items) is a separate semantics question and is out of scope here.

# Create the `pane-triage` skill — gated close of idle panes in the current herdr workspace

## Goal

As a producer running several herdr workspaces, I want a `/skill:pane-triage`
that reports every pane in the invoking workspace, splits them into idle vs
active, surfaces each idle item's producer-review state and a log tail,
recommends the idle panes to close, and closes them **only after my explicit
approval** — so finished dispatch panes stop accumulating and holding memory/CPU.

## Context

- Agents that end with `</end_session>` leave their pane open; these accumulate
  and hold memory (see WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS).
- Existing auto-close work (WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN, WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN) targets
  dispatch panes only and is already completed.
- This skill is the manual, workspace-scoped, approval-gated complement: it
  never closes anything unattended.

## Recommended source location

- **Canonical**: `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/` — `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a
  symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`, so a global skill must live there.
- Assumption: tracked in ContextHub because the herdr pane lifecycle work lives
  here. Confirm whether the skill should instead be ContextHub-local
  (`.pi/skills/pane-triage/`). If ContextHub-local, it will not be globally
  available.

## Skill specification (fixed defaults, no execution-control flags)

**Name / description**

- `name: pane-triage`
- `disable-model-invocation: true`
- description: "Triage and clean up panes in the current herdr workspace: idle
  vs active, producer-review state, log tails, then close idle panes after
  explicit producer approval."

**Scope and terminology**

- Workspace = `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` of the invoking pane (fallback
  `herdr pane current`); the report covers only this workspace.
- Tabs via `herdr tab list --workspace <id>`; panes via
  `herdr pane list --workspace <id>`.
- Idle = the pane's `agent_session.value` file exists and its last non-empty
  JSONL entry is an assistant message whose concatenated `text` blocks
  (`.rstrip()`) end with `</end_session>`.
- Active = any other pane (including plain shells with no session).
- Needs Review = the idle pane's work item has `needsProducerReview == true`
  (`wl show <id> --json`). Work-item id parsed from the trailing
  ` - <PREFIX>-<HASH>` in the pane label.

**Fixed defaults**

- Workspace: invoking workspace only; no cross-workspace roll-up.
- Log tail: 20 lines of the final session message per idle item (no active logs).
- Close recommendation: always emitted.
- Closing: enabled (dry-run off) but only after explicit approval.
- Output: markdown to stdout, pasted verbatim by the invoking agent.

**Algorithm**

1. Resolve workspace and fetch its label/number; error clearly if outside herdr.
2. Enumerate tabs and panes; index panes by tab.
3. Derive `title = label || terminal_title || "(untitled)"`.
4. Classify each pane idle/active; build the Idle and Active tables.
5. Enrich idle panes with work item id and `needsProducerReview` (`n/a` if no id).
6. Print each idle pane's final-message tail under the heading
   `<pane title> Needs Review <true|false>`.
7. Emit the report.
8. Emit the "Recommended to close" table.
9. Ask for producer approval, then close.

**Report structure**

```
# Pane report — <workspace label> (<workspace id>)

## Idle
| Tab | Title | Pane ID | Work item | Needs Review |

## Active
| Tab | Title | Pane ID |

## Idle item logs
### <pane title> Needs Review <true|false>
```text
<last 20 lines of final session message>
```

## Recommended to close
| Title | Pane ID | Work item | Needs Review | Reason |

## Closed
| Pane ID | Result |
```

**Recommend-to-close rules**

- Idle panes → recommended.
- Idle with `needsProducerReview == true` → recommended, annotated `review-pending`.
- Active panes / plain shells → not recommended.
- The invoking pane (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) → never recommended and never closed.

**Approval and closing**

- Mandatory blocking prompt: "N idle panes are recommended to close: <ids>.
  Close them? (yes / select / no)". `no`, or any ambiguity, closes nothing.
- `yes` → close all recommended; `select <ids>` → close only those.
- Immediately before closing, re-read `herdr pane list` and re-classify: drop
  any pane that is no longer idle, is the invoking pane, or no longer exists.
- Close with `herdr pane close <pane_id>`, one at a time; continue on individual
  failure and report a per-pane ledger; non-zero exit if any close failed.
- Idempotent: already-closed panes are skipped.

**Safety contract**

- Never close the invoking pane, under any circumstances.
- No approval → no mutation.
- Never act on the earlier snapshot alone; re-verify before closing.
- Never close more panes than approved.
- No unattended/automatic closing.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `/skill:pane-triage` resolves the invoking workspace from
   `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (fallback `herdr pane current`) and reports only it.
2. Idle classification requires the last non-empty session entry to be an
   assistant message ending with `</end_session>`; a marker quoted mid-message
   does not qualify.
3. The report renders Idle and Active tables (tab, title, pane id) and, for idle
   items, the work item id and `needsProducerReview` value.
4. Each idle item's last 20 log lines are printed under the heading
   `<pane title> Needs Review <true|false>`.
5. A "Recommended to close" table lists idle panes and excludes the invoking
   pane; `needsProducerReview=true` rows are annotated `review-pending`.
6. No pane is closed without explicit producer approval (`yes`/`select`);
   `no`/ambiguity closes nothing; the invoking pane is never closed.
7. Approved panes are re-verified idle immediately before closing; any pane that
   became active is skipped with a reason in the Closed ledger.
8. Offline fixture tests cover classification, marker-mid-message rejection,
   work-item id parsing, `needsProducerReview` mapping, recommendation rules,
   and approval gating (no approval → zero close calls).

## References

- WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS — investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not
  closed on completion (evaluated for deferral to this skill).
- WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN — log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch
  panes, except implement.
- WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN — implement auto-close logic with implement exception.

# Intake Brief: Review Queue depth notification is incorrect (AH-0MUDYTQ55002NUSJ)

## Headline

When the herdr worklist review queue is deep, the footer banner currently always
says "— audits will drain it". It must instead say "— focus on audits" while any
review item still lacks a current audit, and "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" once
every review item is audited.

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist shows a review-queue-depth banner when the root-only
`completed/in_review` count reaches `browseItemCount`. Today the banner copy is
fixed ("… — audits will drain it"), so it gives the same instruction whether
audits are still outstanding or the queue is fully audited and ready to ship.
The copy should reflect the actual audit state so the producer knows whether to
keep running audits or to ship.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — reads the banner to decide the next action.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deep and some items
    still need auditing, I want the banner to say "focus on audits" so I know
    audits are the drain. When every item in the queue has a current audit, I
    want the banner to say "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" so I know I can ship.
- **Downtime dispatcher / operator** — must be unaffected: the banner is
  display-only and never gates dispatch (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the review queue is deep (root-only `completed/in_review` count ≥
   `browseItemCount`) **and** at least one root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Review queue deep (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`.
2. When the review queue is deep **and** no root-level `in_review` item has an

## Goal

As an operator, I want a script that programmatically closes panes whose
sessions are finished or dead, so panes stop accumulating without me clicking
anything (parent AC1, AC2).

Implement the reaper orchestration plus a CLI entrypoint. It lists panes, reads
each session's final assistant message, probes liveness/idle time, classifies

## Constraints

- Never close the invoking pane.
- Never close `implement` panes, `needsProducerReview=true` items, or panes with live children.
- Idempotent: a pane already gone/closed is skipped, not an error.
- Fail-closed: on an ambiguous classification, do not close.

## Goal

As an operator, I do not want orphaned child processes (e.g. audit/plan
runners) reparented to PID 1 when a session closes (parent AC5).

wire it into the reaper's close path.

- Terminate only the target session's process group; never signal unrelated processes.
- Escalate gracefully (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a bounded grace period).
- Never throw when the process group is already gone.

- A new `packages/herdr/src/process-group.ts` exports a teardown helper (e.g. `terminateProcessGroup(pid, opts)`) and is wired into the reaper's close path.

- Teardown is bounded (SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL) and returns a structured result (`terminated` / `already-gone` / `failed`).
- No orphan is reparented to PID 1 in the test (asserted via a process probe, not log text).
- Existing tests remain green.

- Detect the session leader pid; `process.kill(-pid, 'SIGTERM')`, wait, then `SIGKILL` if still alive.

## Moved to llm-manager worklog

Per producer decision, this item is **moved** to the `llm-manager` (LP-) worklog as **LP-0MUJZHTCN006IZRW** — "View Logs Slots tab shows no log output — per-slot SSE streams exceed the browser connection budget".

### Why

The producer clarified the manual-review rejection (truncated in the audit record) as **"There is no output for any slots"** on the View Logs page (`/logs`). Investigation found the root cause in `llm-manager`:

- The page opens 2 raw-pane SSE streams + 1 `/events` status stream + **2 SSE streams per slot**, exceeding the browser's ~6-connection-per-origin limit. With 2-3 configured slots, the overflow `/logs/tail` requests are queued and never deliver data, so most slot panes stay empty.
- Reproduced against a locally served app with 4 slots: the server received only `slot=0` (proxy+llama) and `source=proxy&slot=1`; slots 1-3 panes stayed empty.
- Secondary defect: `proxy/ui.py::tail_logs` `continue`s after each counts/tokens update, starving the log-file follow check during active generation.

The prefill-vs-Working fix (commit `52307b7f`, already on `llm-manager` `origin/dev`) is unrelated to this symptom and remains correct.

### Notes

- No ContextHub source change is required.
- Implementation, tests and release of the fix are tracked under LP-0MUJZHTCN006IZRW in `llm-manager`.
